submission.bindingBasis: Boundary evidence shows currentRevision=3 differs from planning-time expected revision=2, and the active frontier has changed from alpha to beta-concurrent. The owner contract requires expectedRevision to match at checkpoint time, and a stale attempt already returned REVISION_CONFLICT/not_committed. I should reobserve to obtain the revision-coherent current state before deciding whether to checkpoint at alpha-complete or rebase.
submission.rationale: The planning-time evidence (revision=2, frontier=alpha-ready) is now stale: boundary evidence shows currentRevision=3 with frontier=beta-concurrent, and the planning revision attempt already failed with REVISION_CONFLICT/not_committed. The intended consequence — checkpointing alpha as complete without overwriting another participant's newer semantic work — cannot be safely achieved because the active semantic frontier has moved to beta and a newer participant changed the next action. Issuing a checkpoint now would either conflict (stale expectedRevision) or risk overwriting the beta-concurrent work. Reobserving is required to get a revision-coherent current checkpoint and determine whether alpha-complete is still meaningful or whether the plan must be rebased to the new frontier. Acting unbound or with planning binding would risk a false/overwriting consequence given the revision drift and frontier change.
